
[yellow bold]-- DEPRECATION -- iot_device.volt:2[/yellow bold]

Move `chip esp32` to volt.toml: chip = "esp32"

 [dim]1 |[/dim] 
 [dim]2 |[/dim] chip esp32
 [dim]  |[/dim] [yellow]     ^^^^^[/yellow]

[cyan]Hint: The chip declaration will move to volt.toml in a future version.[/cyan]


[yellow bold]-- UNSAVED STORAGE -- iot_device.volt:9[/yellow bold]

Storage variable `readings_count` is never saved, so it resets to its default on every boot.

 [dim]8 |[/dim] 
 [dim]9 |[/dim] storage readings_count: int = 0
 [dim]  |[/dim] [yellow]        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^[/yellow]

[cyan]Hint: Call `storage.save("readings_count", readings_count)` after changing it.[/cyan]


[yellow bold]-- UNHANDLED FAILURE -- iot_device.volt:12[/yellow bold]

`wifi.connect` can fail, and nothing here says what happens then: the program carries on without a connection.

 [dim]11 |[/dim] setup {
 [dim]12 |[/dim]     wifi.connect("MySSID", "MyPass")
 [dim]   |[/dim] [yellow]    ^^^^[/yellow]

[cyan]Hint: Add a fallback: `or retry(5)` to try again, `or skip` to carry on, or `or restart` to reboot.[/cyan]


[yellow bold]-- UNHANDLED FAILURE -- iot_device.volt:13[/yellow bold]

`mqtt.connect` can fail, and nothing here says what happens then: the program carries on without a connection.

 [dim]12 |[/dim]     wifi.connect("MySSID", "MyPass")
 [dim]13 |[/dim]     mqtt.connect("mqtt://broker.local")
 [dim]   |[/dim] [yellow]    ^^^^[/yellow]

[cyan]Hint: Add a fallback: `or retry(5)` to try again, `or skip` to carry on, or `or restart` to reboot.[/cyan]
